q: How do I calculate the carbon footprint of hand sanitizer per litre?
title: Hand sanitizer carbon footprint per litre
short: Alcohol is the main input: multiply the ethanol or isopropyl alcohol per litre by the supplier's figure. Add glycerine, gel agents and the bottle, then blending and filling electricity divided by litres filled.

ul: Ethanol or isopropyl alcohol by volume.

p: Report per litre with alcohol content, and per pack size for retail packs.

example.title: Worked example: hand sanitizer unit per litre (one month)
lines: Plant total: 2,840 / 100,000 = 0.0284 kg CO2 per litre
Add alcohol, additives and bottles for the full figure
example.note: Inputs are illustrative; use your own bills and production records.

senseible: Senseible reads the plant's electricity bills (CEA grid factor 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh, CO2 Baseline Database version 21.0) and fuel invoices (IPCC 2006 defaults) into a fingerprinted Scope 1 and 2 record, the plant-level input to a per-unit figure. Bought-in materials go to the supplier evidence trail; product reports are self-declared drafts.
